cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to Timothy, the man he calls his child. He's just told Timothy to fight the good fight, and now he says 'First of all, then,' so you KNOW this is the top of the list. He urges that petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgiving be offered.

cards.question: Paul wants petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgiving offered. Who are they for?
Then Paul names one group in particular for that prayer list. Which group is it?

answers.text: Kings and all those in authority

cards.text: Kings and all those in authority. Yes, friend, that includes the boss who schedules a meeting at 4:55 on a FRIDAY.

cards.question: Paul says to pray for kings and those in authority so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.

cards.text: Tranquil and quiet. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer next to dead batteries arguing all night about who had the most charge left, so that sounds like a VACATION.

cards.question: How does Paul say this kind of praying for everyone looks in the sight of God our Savior?
Paul says God our Savior wants only certain people to be saved.

cards.text: God our Savior wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Everyone, friend, not just the people who actually reply in the group chat.
Then Paul gives the reason: there is one God. And between God and men, there is one mediator.

cards.question: Paul says there is one mediator between God and men. Who is it?

cards.text: And Christ Jesus doesn't just stand in the middle like a referee. He gives Himself.

cards.question: Paul says Christ Jesus gave Himself as a ___ for all.

cards.text: Paul calls this the testimony given at just the right time. For this reason, he says, he was appointed as a preacher, an apostle and a teacher.

cards.question: Paul says he was appointed as a faithful and true teacher of the ___.

cards.text: Then Paul adds, "I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything." Friend, I say that every time I tell a baker I only tasted ONE chocolate chip, and Paul's the one of us who actually means it.
Next Paul turns to the men everywhere. He wants them to pray, lifting up holy hands.

cards.question: Paul wants the men everywhere to pray with holy hands lifted up. What does he want that praying to be without?

cards.text: So no praying with one hand lifted up and the other one honking at the guy who just cut you off. BOTH hands, friend. Holy ones.
Then Paul turns to the women. He wants them to dress respectably, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes.

cards.question: Instead of braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes, what does Paul want the women adorned with?
Paul says good deeds are proper for women who profess to worship God.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness."

cards.question: Paul says there are two things he does not permit a woman to do. What are they?

answers.text: Teach or exercise authority over a man
Own land or run a business of her own
Travel or trade in the market alone

cards.text: She is to remain quiet, Paul says. Then he gives a reason that goes all the way back to the beginning.

cards.question: Paul says ___ was formed first and then ___.
Paul says it was Adam who was deceived and fell into transgression.

cards.text: Then Paul ends with a word for women. He says they will be saved through childbearing, and then he adds an if.

cards.question: Paul says women will be saved through childbearing if they continue in something. What is it?

answers.text: Faith and love and holiness with self-control
Prayer and fasting and patience with others
Hope and joy and gentleness with everyone

findings.problem: The card states two facts from outside the passage: Paul calls Timothy his child (1 Timothy 1:2), and he has just told Timothy to fight the good fight (1 Timothy 1:18). It cites only 1 Timothy 2:1, so neither fact carries its reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Fellow believers' is included in 'everyone'. A baker could argue that Paul's prayers are for fellow believers.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer to card 3 ('Kings and all those in authority') and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage and does not move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card only repeats 'Tranquil and quiet' from the card 5 statement and adds a junk drawer joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap card for a joke.
The card only restates the card 2 answer (praying without anger) through a joke. It adds nothing new from 1 Timothy 2:8 and does not move the passage along.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 9 says the reason 'goes all the way back to the beginning', which rules out Noah. Eve is also the only woman among the five words, in a section about women, so blank 2 is obvious.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells the rest of 1 Timothy 2:14, that the woman was deceived and fell into transgression. A false true or false answer only tells the baker the statement about Adam is not right, so an important detail of the passage is missed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The statement joins 'deceived' and 'fell into transgression'. Marking it false suggests Adam did not fall into transgression, but the passage leaves that open (Romans 5:14 speaks of Adam's transgression). Only 'deceived' is false here.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 12 says 'he adds an if', and the question asks what comes next. The answers are three lists of virtues, so the baker can only guess the wording of the rest of the line. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason out faith, love and holiness over the others.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
